cim: AI mental health regulatory sandbox will make digital support safer
cim_eredeti: AI mental health regulatory sandbox will make digital support safer
szoveg_eredeti:
The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) and the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) announced the launch of the AI in Mental Health Airlock on 23 November 2026.

The project aims to support innovation while ensuring appropriate safeguards protect patients and the public.

The AI in Mental Health Airlock will bring together regulators, technology developers, healthcare professionals and people with lived experience to explore how AI-powered mental health tools should be assessed and regulated.

AI is increasingly being used to provide mental health support, with technologies ranging from therapeutic chatbots to virtual reality tools designed to support psychological treatment.

Recent research suggests that more than one in three adults (37%) have used an AI chatbot to support their mental health or wellbeing.

Health Innovation Minister James Frith said:

“AI has the potential to open up new ways for people to access mental health support, but innovation must go hand in hand with safety and public confidence.

“We want to support the development of AI that makes a real difference to people’s lives, while ensuring patients can have confidence in the technologies designed to support their mental health.”

While these technologies could improve access to support and help healthcare services reach more people, questions remain around their safety, effectiveness, reliability and the handling of personal information.

Some AI chatbots may fall under medical device regulations, depending on their intended purpose, while others may not. The new initiative aims to help clarify how these products should be evaluated.

The AI in Mental Health Airlock builds on the MHRA’s existing AI Airlock programme and forms part of a wider Wellcome-funded project, first launched in 2023.

Working alongside NICE’s Health Technology Innovation Assessment Lab, the sandbox will explore the challenges of assessing AI technologies in mental healthcare and identify proportionate approaches to regulation and evidence gathering.

Up to five organisations will be selected to participate. They will work with experts, clinicians, regulators and people with lived experience through workshops and testing activities.

The AI in Mental Health Airlock aims to clarify regulatory expectations while helping ensure new technologies are supported by robust evidence and appropriate safeguards.

Organisations interested in taking part can find application details through the government’s website: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/apply-for-the-ai-in-mental-health-airlock
